title: How to Learn SQL: A Beginner's Roadmap for 2026
dek: You can learn enough SQL to be useful in 4 to 8 weeks by focusing on six core commands, practicing on a real database daily, and skipping the advanced topics until you actually need them.

seo.metaTitle: How to Learn SQL: A Beginner's Roadmap (2026)
seo.metaDescription: A focused, no-fluff roadmap to learn SQL from scratch — the six commands that matter, a weekly plan, free practice tools, and how long it really takes.

sources.label: MDN Web Docs — Databases and SQL basics

body.richText: SQL is the language you use to ask a database questions. It is the highest-return skill for anyone working with data, and it is far easier to learn than a general-purpose programming language because the core is small and readable. The trap beginners fall into is trying to learn all of it. You do not need to.
Learn these six things well before anything else: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, JOIN, GROUP BY, and aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG). That covers the vast majority of real analyst queries.

body.text: The six commands that matter first

body.caption: The core SQL you need before anything advanced.
rows: Combine rows from two or more tables
Collapse rows into groups for aggregation

richText: A query that uses most of these at once looks like this — and if you can read and write it comfortably, you already know enough to be useful:

body.content:
SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS people, AVG(salary) AS avg_salary
FROM employees
WHERE active = true
GROUP BY department
ORDER BY avg_salary DESC;

items: Week 1: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY on a single table until they are automatic
Week 2: JOINs — the concept that trips up most beginners; practice until it clicks
Week 3: GROUP BY and aggregate functions; combine them with WHERE and JOIN
Week 4: subqueries and CASE; start solving practice problems from scratch
Weeks 5-8: daily practice on real, messy datasets and interview-style questions

body.richText: The single most effective habit is writing SQL every day against a real database, not just watching lessons. Reading SQL and writing SQL are different skills, and only the second one shows up in interviews.

items: SQLite — zero setup, runs anywhere, perfect for a first database
PostgreSQL — the free, production-grade database worth learning on
Any interactive SQL practice site with a built-in editor and sample data
A public dataset you actually care about, loaded into your own database

body.text: How long does it really take?

body.richText: To be useful for analyst work: 4 to 8 weeks of consistent daily practice. To be genuinely strong, including window functions and query optimization: a few more months of real use on the job. You do not need the advanced material to start applying or to pass most entry-level screens.

items.question: Is SQL hard to learn?
items.answerRichText: No, not by programming standards. The syntax reads almost like English and the core is small. JOINs and GROUP BY take the most practice, but most people are writing useful queries within a few weeks.

items.question: How long does it take to learn SQL for a job?
items.answerRichText: About 4 to 8 weeks of daily practice to reach a useful, interview-ready level with the core commands. Deeper mastery comes with real work over the following months.

items.question: Should I learn SQL or Python first?
answerRichText: For data analyst roles, learn SQL first — it is required almost everywhere and faster to become useful in. Add Python afterward; see our guide on
